title: Alternating Suffixes
author: codex:gpt-6.1-sol
statement:
# Alternating Suffixes

There are cells numbered from 0 to n and m distinguishable tokens. Every token has a mode, either 0 or 1. Cell 0 is terminal in both modes.

For each cell i > 0, two integers L[i][0] and L[i][1] are given. On a turn, choose one token at cell i > 0 in mode c, choose an integer j with L[i][c] <= j < i, and move that token to cell j in mode 1-c. Other tokens do not change. When L[i][c] = i, this token has no legal move. Tokens may share a cell and do not block each other.

Two players alternate turns. A player with no legal move loses. Count the legal first moves after which the next player loses under optimal play. Moves that choose different tokens are different, even if those tokens have identical states. For a fixed token, different destination cells are different moves.

## Input

The first line contains n and m.

The next n lines contain L[i][0] and L[i][1], in increasing order of i.

The next m lines contain p and c, the initial cell and mode of a token.

## Output

Print the number of winning first moves as an integer.

## Constraints

- 1 <= n, m <= 100000.
- 0 <= L[i][c] <= i.
- 0 <= p <= n and c is 0 or 1.

## Examples

### Example 1
Input
```text
1 1
1 1
1 0
```
Output
```text
0
```

### Example 2
Input
```text
1 3
0 0
1 0
1 1
1 0
```
Output
```text
3
```
Any first move leaves exactly two movable tokens.

### Example 3
Input
```text
2 2
0 0
0 1
2 0
1 0
```
Output
```text
1
```
The only winning move sends the first token to cell 1 in mode 1.
